overview.body:
**Belobog** ​(*belobog*) ‌— Light, ‌Good, ​Fortune ​· ​White ​god — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Slavic tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Light, ​Good, ​Fortune". The ​name ‌means ​"White ‌god".

**Belobog** ​is ‌light, ​good, ‌fortune. ​The name ‌means ​"White ​god" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​slavic ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**Belobog** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/belobog/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*belobog* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this ​name; **Belobog** ​is ​a scholarly ​transliteration ‌of the ​reconstructed ​spoken form. ‌Etymologically ​the name ‌means ​"White god".

‌The ​ASCII form ​*belobog* ​survives only ​because ​the early ‌domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ‌diacritics; it ​is ‌a technological ​compromise, ‌not an ​ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ‌restoration **Belobog** ‌recovers ​the full ​diacritic ‌detail of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly ​in the ​address ‌bar. The ​restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ​letters or ​diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in Tier ‌2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ​**b** ‌→ **B** ​— ​Same
- ​**e** ‌→ ​**e** — ​Same
​- **l** ‌→ ​**l** — ​Same
​- **o** ‌→ ​**o** — ‌Same
​- **b** ‌→ ​**b** — ‌Same
‌- **o** ​→ ​**o** — ​Same
​- **g** ‌→ ‌**g** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/belobog/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**belobog** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Belobog.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"belobog" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Belobog".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"belobog" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Belobog" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Belobog was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Belobog ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Belobog ‌place ​light, good, ​fortune ​at the ​center ​of ‌a living ​mythological ​world.

‌### Origins ​(Myth)

‌Belobog appears ​in ‌slavic ​tradition as ​light, ​good, fortune. ​The ​name's ‌meaning, "White ​god", ‌shapes ​the narratives ‌told ​about this ‌figure.

​### ‌Worship and ​Memory ​(Cult)

Devotees ‌and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ​Belobog ​in ‌ritual, text, ​and ​iconography, ensuring ‌the ​name ​survived into ‌the ​modern scholarly ‌record.

​The ​myths of ​Belobog ​survive in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, ​and later ‌retellings. ​Each ​version reflects ‌the ‌interests of ‌its ‌tellers ​— poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The ‌PuniCodex entry ​does ​not ​privilege a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the ‌attestations so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Belobog ‌gives ​the figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Belobog ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Belobog, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​light ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Belobog is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of light, ​Good, ‌Fortune ​in ​the ‌mind and ​to ‌ask ​what ‌of it ​endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"White god" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​light, ‌Good, ​Fortune ​· ‌White god.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Belobog ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*belobog* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
